model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of different levels of ambiguity, categorized by standard deviation (SD) for outer ambiguity and maximum value (Max) for inner ambiguity. There are five categories of ambiguity based on standard deviation: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94 for the outer ambiguity and three categories for the inner ambiguity: 1, 2, and 3. The largest portion of the chart is dedicated to the ambiguity category with a standard deviation of 0.82, constituting 47.7% of the outer ambiguity. The category with the smallest portion is the standard deviation of 0.47, making up 7.0% of the outer ambiguity. The inner ambiguity shows a more evenly distributed pattern, with the maximum ambiguity levels of 1 and 2 both taking up 14.2%, and level 3 being the most common at 39.0%. To summarize, the chart reveals that while the outer ambiguity is mostly concentrated in the middle range deviations, the inner ambiguity has a higher proportion of levels 1 and 2.
